name: Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

**Śrī Rūpa-mañjarī**, the foremost of Śrī Rādhā's mañjarīs.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 180

> śrī-rūpa-mañjarī khyātā yāsīd vṛndāvane purā
> sādya rūpākhya-gosvāmī bhūtvā prakaṭatām iyāt

«Śrī Rūpa-mañjarī, who had been famous in Vṛndāvana-dhāma, appeared as Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī.»

## Rūpa-mañjarī in the books

- **Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā** (Laghu-bhāga 182–184): first in the list of Śrī Rādhā's mañjarīs — Rūpa, Rāga, Rati, Lavaṅga, Guṇa, Rasa, Vilāsa, Prema, Maṇi, Suvarṇa, Kāma, Ratna, Kastūrī, Gandha, Netra, Padma, Līlā and Hema-mañjarī.
- **Mañjarī-svarūpa-nirūpaṇa** (Ananta dāsa Bābājī): Rūpa-mañjarī, Rati-mañjarī, Guṇa-mañjarī and the others are Rādhā's sakhīs who act as her confidential handmaidens. The Govinda-līlāmṛta (1.86) calls Rūpa-mañjarī Rādhā's *priya-narma-sakhī*, her «most dear pleasure companion». Narottama dāsa (Prema-bhakti-candrikā): «Of them the best is Rūpa Mañjarī; Rati Mañjarī is also noteworthy, as are Lavaṅga Mañjarī and Mañjulālī.»
- Her name: the mañjarīs are named for qualities that come from Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī's own, so Rūpa-mañjarī's beauty (*rūpa*) is equal to Rādhā's; or else the beauty and sweetness of all the mañjarīs comes from Śrī Rūpa-mañjarī's (Mañjarī-svarūpa-nirūpaṇa).
- In the līlā she leads the service: at her hint Rati-mañjarī serves Rādhā, and the practitioner prays to stand behind Śrī Rūpa-mañjarī; following her is the essence of rāgānuga-bhakti (Mañjarī-svarūpa-nirūpaṇa).
- Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, introduction: «internally, in his siddha-deha», Rūpa Gosvāmī serves under the guidance of Śrī Lalitā, Śrī Viśākhā and Śrī Rūpa-mañjarī herself.

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā of Kavi Karṇapūra, 180; Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā of Śrīla Rūpa Gosvāmī (ed. Bhaktivedānta Nārāyaṇa Gosvāmī), Laghu-bhāga 182–184; Mañjarī-svarūpa-nirūpaṇa of Ananta dāsa Bābājī.
remove: In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Rūpa Mañjarī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 180).

name: Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

**Śrī Rati-mañjarī**, also called **Lavaṅga-mañjarī**, Rūpa-mañjarī's dearest friend; **Sanātana Kumāra**, the jewel among sages, also entered him.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 181–182

> sā rūpa-mañjarī-preṣṭhā purāsīd rati-mañjarī
> socyate nāma-bhedena lavaṅga-mañjarī budhaiḥ
> sādya gaurābhinna-tanuḥ sarvārādhyaḥ sanātanaḥ
> tam eva prāviśat kāryān muni-ratnaḥ sanātanaḥ

«Rūpa-mañjarī's closest friend, who was known by the names Rati-mañjarī and Lavaṅga-mañjarī, appeared as Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmī, who was honoured by everyone and considered like an extension of the transcendental body of Lord Caitanya. Sanātana Kumāra, the jewel among the sages, entered the body of Sanātana Gosvāmī, who is therefore also considered an incarnation of Sanātana Kumāra.»

## Rati-mañjarī in the books

- **Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā** (Laghu-bhāga 182–184): among Śrī Rādhā's mañjarīs; Rati-mañjarī and Prema-mañjarī are both also known as **Bhānumatī**. Lavaṅga-mañjarī is named in the same list.
- **Mañjarī-svarūpa-nirūpaṇa**: the Govinda-līlāmṛta (2.52) calls Rati-mañjarī Rādhā's *sakhī*; Narottama dāsa: «Rati Mañjarī is also noteworthy… Kasturikā Mañjarī and others happily serve along with Śrī Rati Mañjarī.» In the līlā: after Rādhā's bath Rati-mañjarī takes off her wet garments and dresses her in a fresh silk sāṛī; she offers camphored pān from a jewelled box, and at Rūpa-mañjarī's hint undoes Rādhā's braid.
- Lavaṅga-mañjarī: one day Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī sent her to bring Kṛṣṇa (Mañjarī-svarūpa-nirūpaṇa).

## Other opinions

Some texts of this record also named Rāga-mañjarī; the Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā gives Rati- / Lavaṅga-mañjarī.

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 181–182; Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, Laghu-bhāga 182–184; Mañjarī-svarūpa-nirūpaṇa of Ananta dāsa Bābājī.
remove: In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Rati Mañjarī (also said to be Rāga or Lavanga Mañjarī).
In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Rati-mañjarī, also called Lavaṅga-mañjarī; Sanātana Kumāra also entered him (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 181-182).

name: Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

**Śrī Vilāsa-mañjarī**, a maidservant of Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 194–207

Kavi Karṇapūra gives a list of Śrī Rādhā's maidservants who, «assuming male forms, appeared among Lord Caitanya's associates, each displaying his particular kind of ecstatic love»: Mālatī, Candralatikā, Mañjumedhā, Varāṅgadā, Ratnāvalī, Kamalā, Guṇacūḍā, Sukeśinī, Karpūra-mañjarī, Śyāma-mañjarī, Śveta-mañjarī, **Vilāsa-mañjarī**, Kamalekhā… They became, in the same order, Śubhānanda dvija, Śrīdhara Brahmacārī, Paramānanda Gupta, Raghunātha dvija, Kaṁsāri Sena, Jagannātha Sena, Subuddhi Miśra, Śrīharṣa, Raghu Miśra, Jitamitra, Bhāgavatācārya, **«Śrīman Jīva Paṇḍita, the saintly son of Śrī Vallabha»**, Vāṇīnātha dvija…

> … suśīlaḥ paṇḍitaḥ śrīmān jīvaḥ śrī-vallabhātmajaḥ …

Śrī Vallabha is Anupama, the youngest brother of Rūpa and Sanātana: so the twelfth maidservant, Vilāsa-mañjarī, is Śrīla Jīva Gosvāmī.

## Vilāsa-mañjarī in the books

- **Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā** (Laghu-bhāga 182–184): among Śrī Rādhā's mañjarīs, after Rūpa, Rāga, Rati, Lavaṅga, Guṇa and Rasa-mañjarī.

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 194–207; Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, Laghu-bhāga 182–184.
remove: In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Vilāsa Mañjarī.

name: Śrīla Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

**Śrī Rasa-mañjarī**. Some say **Rati-mañjarī**, others **Bhānumatī**.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 186

> dāsa-śrī-raghunāthasya pūrvākhyā rasa-mañjarī
> amuṁ kecit prabhāṣante śrīmatīṁ rati-mañjarīm
> bhānumaty-ākhyayā kecid āhus taṁ nāma-bhedataḥ

«Śrīla Raghunātha dāsa Gosvāmī was the incarnation of Rasa-mañjarī. Some say that he was Rati-mañjarī, and others say he was the incarnation of Bhānumatī.»

## In the books

- **Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā** (Laghu-bhāga 182–184): Rasa-mañjarī and Rati-mañjarī are both among Śrī Rādhā's mañjarīs, and Rati-mañjarī is also known by the name **Bhānumatī** — so the three names of the verse may point to one person.
- **Mañjarī-svarūpa-nirūpaṇa**: in his Muktā-carita, Raghunātha dāsa calls Raṅgaṇamālā and Tulasī-mañjarī Rādhā's *parama-praṇayī-sakhīs*, «most loving friends».

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 186; Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, Laghu-bhāga 182–184; Mañjarī-svarūpa-nirūpaṇa.
remove: In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Rāsa Mañjarī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 186; some say Rati Mañjarī or Bhanumati).
In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Rasa-mañjarī (others: Rati-mañjarī or Bhānumatī) (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 186).

name: Śrī Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

**Śrī Rāga-mañjarī**.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 185

> raghunāthākhyako bhaṭṭaḥ purā yā rāga-mañjarī
> kṛta-śrī-rādhikā-kuṇḍa-kuṭīra-vasatiḥ sa tu

«Rāga-mañjarī appeared as Śrīla Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī, who lived in a cottage by the shore of Rādhā-kuṇḍa.»

## Rāga-mañjarī in the books

- **Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā** (Laghu-bhāga 182–184): the second in the list of Śrī Rādhā's mañjarīs, after Rūpa-mañjarī.

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 185; Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, Laghu-bhāga 182–184.
remove: In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Rāga Mañjarī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā).
In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Rāga-mañjarī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 185).

name: Śrī Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

**Śrī Anaṅga-mañjarī**, Śrī Rādhā's younger sister. Some say **Guṇa-mañjarī**.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 184

> anaṅga-mañjarī yāsīt sādya gopāla-bhaṭṭakaḥ
> bhaṭṭa-gosvāminaṁ kecid āhuḥ śrī-guṇa-mañjarīm

«Anaṅga-mañjarī appeared as Śrīla Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī. Some say that Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī was actually the incarnation of Śrī Guṇa-mañjarī.»

## Anaṅga-mañjarī in the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā

> vasanta-ketakī-kāntir mañjulānaṅga-mañjarī
> yathārthākṣara-nāmeyam indīvara-nibhāmbarā
> durmado madavān asyāḥ patir yo devaraḥ svasuḥ
> priyāsau lalitā-devyā viśākhāyā viśeṣataḥ (Bṛhad-bhāga 121–122)

- **Śrī Rādhā's younger sister** (Laghu-bhāga 173a: «Śrī Rādhā's elder brother is Śrīdāmā and Her younger sister is Anaṅga-mañjarī»).
- **Complexion**: like a spring ketakī flower. **Dress**: the colour of a blue lotus.
- Even Anaṅga (Cupid) is attracted by her beauty and sweetness, so her name fits her.
- **Husband**: the proud Durmada, younger brother of Śrī Rādhā's husband.
- Extremely dear to **Lalitā-devī**, and especially to **Viśākhā**.
- She is counted among the exalted (*vara*) sakhīs of Rādhā's own age.

## Guṇa-mañjarī

Guṇa-mañjarī is fifth in Rādhā's list of mañjarīs (Laghu-bhāga 182). The Govinda-līlāmṛta (1.87) calls her Rādhā's *dāsikā*, maidservant; Maṇi-mañjarī is her follower (Mañjarī-svarūpa-nirūpaṇa). His disciple Śrīnivāsa Ācārya is Maṇi-mañjarī, serving under Guṇa-mañjarī (Nandgram Dham).

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 184; Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, Bṛhad-bhāga 121–122, Laghu-bhāga 173, 182; Mañjarī-svarūpa-nirūpaṇa.
remove: In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Anaṅga Mañjarī (some say Guṇa Mañjarī).
In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Anaṅga-mañjarī (some say Guṇa-mañjarī) (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 184).

name: Śrī Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

**Śrī Viśākhā**, the second of Śrī Rādhā's eight principal sakhīs, who taught Rādhā the fine arts.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 160

> kalām aśikṣayad rādhāṁ yā viśākhā vraje purā
> sādya svarūpa-gosvāmī tat-tad-bhāva-vilāsavān

«Śrīmatī Viśākhā-gopī, who formerly taught the various fine arts to Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī in Vrajabhūmi, appeared during Lord Caitanya's advent as Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī, who was filled with the various splendid manifestations of ecstatic love of God.»

## Viśākhā in the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā

> viśākhātra dvitīyā syād ekācāra-guṇa-vratā
> priya-sakhyā janir yatra tatraiṣābhyuditā kṣaṇe (Bṛhad-bhāga 83)

- The second of the eight *variṣṭha* sakhīs; like Śrī Rādhā in conduct, qualities and determination in serving Kṛṣṇa. **She was born at exactly the same moment as Śrī Rādhikā.**
- **Complexion**: like lightning. **Dress**: like the sky set with stars — blue, embroidered with white flowers and leaves.
- **Father**: Pāvana, son of Mukharā's sister. **Mother**: Dakṣiṇā, daughter of Jaṭilā's sister. **Husband**: Vāhika Gopa (84–85).
- In her fresh youth; a *priya-narma-sakhī* (also called *parama-preṣṭha-sakhī*), faultless in advice, expert in joking words before Govinda, in understanding the hearts of Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa and in carrying their messages, and in every means of bringing them together (165–166).
- Her arts: painting designs of creepers and flowers with red ochre on the body, stringing garlands and flower crowns, drawing *sarvato-bhadra-maṇḍalas* and composing poems in that style with double meanings, preparing the worship of the Sun-god, singing songs of many lands and in *dhrupada*, and writing poetry (167–169a).
- Under her serve Raṅgāvalī and other sakhīs expert in painting, Mādhavī, Mālatī, Candrarekhā and others, and the sakhīs and maidservants in charge of clothing (169b–170).

## Other opinions

The notes of this record had «Lalitā» (and named this verse 160 for it); the Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā says **Viśākhā**, and this book is followed here. Dhyānacandra Gosvāmī is said to give Lalitā; Nandgram Dham gives Viśākhā («some call him Lalitā»).

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 160; Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, Bṛhad-bhāga 83–85, 165–170.
remove: In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Lalitā Sakhī (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 160; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).
The record's text gave Viśākhā, and Lalitā according to Dhyānacandra Gosvāmī.
Nandgram Dham gives his identity as Viśākhā, who taught Rādhā the arts; some call him Lalitā.

name: Rāmānanda Rāya
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

Three persons in one: **Arjuna**, Kṛṣṇa's cowherd friend (*priya-narma-sakhā*) in Vṛndāvana; **Arjuna the Pāṇḍava**; and the gopī **Arjunīyā**. Some say **Lalitā**.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 120–124

> priya-narma-sakhaḥ kaścid arjunaḥ pāṇḍavo 'rjunaḥ
> militvā samabhūd rāmānanda-rāyaḥ prabhoḥ priyaḥ (120)

«The cowherd boy Arjuna, who was a close friend of the Lord in Vṛndāvana, and the Pāṇḍava Arjuna both joined to become Rāmānanda Rāya, who was very dear to Lord Caitanya.»

> ato rādhā-kṛṣṇa-bhakti-prema-tattvādikaṁ kṛtī
> rāmānando gauracandraṁ pratyavarṇayad anvaham (121)

«This exalted personality, Rāmānanda Rāya, for many days described to Lord Caitanya the true nature of pure love for Śrī Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa.»

122–124: «Some say that Rāmānanda Rāya is the incarnation of Lalitā-gopī, and others say that because Lord Caitanya directly told Rāmānanda Rāya's father, Bhavānanda Rāya, that he was the incarnation of Mahārāja Pāṇḍu, Rāmānanda Rāya must be the incarnation of the Pāṇḍava Arjuna. The most learned devotees say that Rāmānanda Rāya is the incarnation of Arjunīyā-gopī, and as the Padma Purāṇa (Uttara-khaṇḍa) shows, the Pāṇḍava Arjuna also became Arjunīyā; therefore Rāmānanda Rāya is all three.»

## Other opinions

The notes of this record had «Viśākhā Sakhī»: the Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā does not say so (Viśākhā is Svarūpa Dāmodara, verse 160), and this book is followed here.

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 120–124.
replace: In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Viśākhā Sakhī; also Arjuna, the Pāṇḍava and Kṛṣṇa's priya-narma-sakhā, and the gopī Arjunīyā (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 120-124; Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava Abhidhāna).
remove: Some say Lalitā, but this is not accepted by all.

name: Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

**Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī**, the queen of Vṛndāvana; **Lalitā** also entered him. Gadādhara is the *bhakta-śakti*, the devotional energy, of the Pañca-tattva.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 11

> bhakta-śaktir dvijāgraṇyaḥ śrī-gadādhara-paṇḍitaḥ

«The devotional energy is Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita, the best of the brāhmaṇas.»

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 147–153

> śrī-rādhā prema-rūpā yā purā vṛndāvaneśvarī
> sā śrī-gadādharo gaura-vallabhaḥ paṇḍitākhyakaḥ (147)

«Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, who is the personification of pure love for Lord Kṛṣṇa and the queen of Vṛndāvana, appeared as Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita, who was very dear to Lord Caitanya.»

148–150: «Śrīla Svarūpa Dāmodara Gosvāmī has also confirmed that the goddess of fortune who appeared in Vṛndāvana and was very dear to Kṛṣṇa has now appeared as Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita, filled with love for Lord Caitanya. Lalitā-gopī always follows Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, and therefore she is known as Anurādhā; when Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī appeared as Gadādhara Paṇḍita, Lalitā followed her, entering his body.»

> iyam api lalitaiva rādhikālī
> na khalu gadādhara eṣa bhūsurendraḥ
> harir ayam atha vā svayaiva śaktyā
> tritayam abhūt sa sakhī ca rādhikā ca (151, from the Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka)

«Gadādhara, the best of the brāhmaṇas, is the incarnation of both Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī and Lalitā-gopī… Gadādhara is therefore the incarnation of three persons: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, Lalitā-gopī and Lord Hari.»

152–153: «Some say that Dhruvānanda Brahmacārī is the incarnation of Lalitā-gopī. This opinion is also correct, for Lalitā appeared as both Gadādhara Paṇḍita and Dhruvānanda Brahmacārī. By His own will Lord Caitanya appeared in three forms at the same time; in the same way Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī appeared as Gadādhara Paṇḍita.»

## Śrī Rādhā in the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā

- In Her prime youth of **fifteen years** (Laghu-bhāga 167). Yaśodā has more love for Her than unlimited mothers could have.
- **Father**: Vṛṣabhānu Mahārāja; **mother**: Kīrtidā-sundarī, also called Ratnagarbhā. Paternal grandparents Mahībhānu and Sukhadā; maternal grandparents Indu and Mukharā. Elder brother **Śrīdāmā**; younger sister **Anaṅga-mañjarī**. Mother-in-law Jaṭilā; Abhimanyu only imagines himself Her husband; Kuṭilā, His sister-in-law, is always looking for faults (168–174).
- Her feet bear the conch, moon, elephant, barley corn, goad, chariot, flag, ḍamaru, svastika and fish (166).

## Lalitā in the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā

- The foremost of the eight sakhīs, **twenty-seven days older than Śrī Rādhā**; renowned as **Anurādhā**; a *vāmā* and *prakharā* heroine (Bṛhad-bhāga 80–81).
- **Complexion**: bright yellow, like gorocanā. **Dress**: the colour of a peacock's tail.
- **Mother**: Sāradī; **father**: Viśoka; **husband**: Bhairava, a friend of Govardhana Gopa (82).
- Leader of all the *parama-preṣṭha* sakhīs; knows all of Rādhā's and Kṛṣṇa's emotions, arranges Their meetings and Their loving quarrels (129–130).

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 11, 147–153; Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, Bṛhad-bhāga 80–82, 129–130, Laghu-bhāga 163–174.
remove: In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Śrīmatī Rādhārāṇī, with Lalitā entering him (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 147-153).

name: Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

**Śrī Balarāma** (Halāyudha), the *bhakta-svarūpa* of the Pañca-tattva; non-different from **Saṅkarṣaṇa**; as **Ananta Śeṣa** He becomes the couch, garments and ornaments of the Lord. **Viśvarūpa** entered Him.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 11

> bhakta-svarūpo nityānando vraje yaḥ śrī-halāyudhaḥ

«The bhakta-svarūpa is Nityānanda, who in Vraja is Śrī Halāyudha [Balarāma].»

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 58–64

- 58–61: Śrī Viśvarūpa is non-different from Saṅkarṣaṇa, the second member of the catur-vyūha; and Lord Nityānanda Avadhūta is also non-different from Saṅkarṣaṇa (Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka: «nityānandāvadhūto mahā iti mahitaṁ hanta saṅkarṣaṇo yaḥ»).
- 62: «When the eternal Personality of Godhead Lord Viśvarūpa disappeared from home, He entered the body of Lord Nityānanda Avadhūta.»
- 63: Kavi Karṇapūra's father, Śivānanda Sena, once said: «Lord Nityānanda Avadhūta is actually the Personality of Godhead Lord Balarāma. Always staying among the devotees, He shines with the splendour of thousands of suns» — and saying this he began to dance.
- 64: «Lord Nityānanda incarnates as His plenary expansion Ananta Śeṣa. As Lord Śeṣa He transforms His body to become the garments, bracelets and other ornaments worn by Lord Viṣṇu and Lord Kṛṣṇa. Expanding again as the pastime-potency, līlā-śakti, Lord Śeṣa is aware of all the details of Lord Kṛṣṇa's confidential pastimes.»

## Śrī Balarāma in the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā

- **Complexion**: white like crystal or camphor. Called Balarāma for His great strength (*bala*). **Dress**: blue, with garlands of forest flowers (Laghu-bhāga 66).
- Long, charming hair with a topknot; jewelled kuṇḍalas; garlands and jewelled necklaces, armlets, bracelets and jewelled ankle-bells (67–69).
- **Father**: Vasudeva, friend of Nanda Mahārāja; **mother**: the chaste Rohiṇī, Yaśodā's friend. Śrī Kṛṣṇa is His younger brother and Subhadrā His sister (69–70).
- Radiant in His youth of **sixteen years**; very dear to Kṛṣṇa and a mine of ecstatic pastimes (71).

## His twelve gopālas (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 126–132)

Abhirāma Ṭhākura (Śrīdāmā), Sundarānanda Ṭhākura (Sudāmā), Dhanañjaya Paṇḍita (Vasudāmā), Gaurīdāsa Paṇḍita (Subala), Kamalākara Pippalāi (Mahābala), Uddhāraṇa Datta (Subāhu), Maheśa Paṇḍita (Mahābāhu), Puruṣottama dāsa (Stoka-kṛṣṇa), Nāgara Puruṣottama (Dāma), Parameśvara dāsa (Arjuna), Kālā Kṛṣṇadāsa (Lavaṅga) — and Kholāvecā Śrīdhara (Kusumāsava, verse 133).

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 11, 58–64, 126–133; Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā, Laghu-bhāga 66–71.

The twelve gopālas (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 126-132; exact names): Abhirāma Ṭhākura (Śrīdāmā), Sundarānanda Ṭhākura (Sudāmā), Dhananjaya (Vasudāmā), Gaurī Dāsa Paṇḍit (Subala), Kamalakara Pippalai (Mahābala), Uddhāraṇa Datta Ṭhākura (Subāhu), Maheśa Paṇḍita (Mahābāhu), Puruṣottama Dāsa (Dāma), Parameśvara Dāsa Ṭhākura (Arjuna), Kālīya Kṛṣṇa Dāsa Ṭhākura (Lavaṅga), Kholāvecā Śrīdhara (Kusumāsava).

name: Śrī Advaita Ācārya Prabhu
text:
## In Kṛṣṇa-līlā

The *bhakta-avatāra* of the Pañca-tattva: **Mahā-Viṣṇu**, one with **Sadāśiva**; by Kṛṣṇa's mercy Sadāśiva also took the form of a **cowherd boy** and danced with Kṛṣṇa in Vraja.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 11

> bhaktāvatāra ācāryo 'dvaito yaḥ śrī-sadāśivaḥ

«The devotional incarnation is Advaita Ācārya, who is Śrī Sadāśiva.»

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 76–80

- 76: «Lord Sadāśiva, who formerly appeared as an āveśa incarnation in Vrajabhūmi, appeared in Lord Caitanya's pastimes as Lord Advaita Gosvāmī, who is non-different from Lord Caitanya Himself.»
- 77–80 (from the Śiva-tantra, Bhairava to Pārvatī): «One day, during the great festival of lights in the month of Kārttika, Lord Kṛṣṇa enthusiastically danced with Lord Balarāma and Their cowherd friends. My dear Pārvatī, when Lord Sadāśiva, my spiritual master, saw this dancing, He yearned to become a cowherd boy and dance with Kṛṣṇa, and began to dance, whirling like a wheel. By Lord Kṛṣṇa's mercy Sadāśiva was able to appear in two forms: in one He remained as Lord Sadāśiva, and in the other He appeared as a cowherd boy in Vraja.»

> ekadā kārttike māsi dīpa-yātrā-mahotsave
> sa-rāmaḥ saha-gopālaḥ kṛṣṇo nṛtyati yatnavān (78)
> śrī-kṛṣṇasya prasādena dvi-vidho 'bhūt sadāśivaḥ
> ekas tatra śivaḥ sākṣād anyo gopāla-vigrahaḥ (80)

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 11, 76–80.
remove: In Kṛṣṇa-līlā: Sadāśiva (with Mahā-Viṣṇu), who also danced in Vraja as a cowherd boy (Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 76-80).

name: Śrīla Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita
text:
## In the līlā

**Nārada Muni**, the best of the sages; the *bhakta* (pure devotee) of the Pañca-tattva. His younger brother Śrī Rāma Paṇḍita was Nārada's friend **Parvata Muni**.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 90

> śrīvāsa-paṇḍito dhīmān yaḥ purā nārado muniḥ
> parvatākhyo muni-varo ya āsīn nārada-priyaḥ
> sa rāma-paṇḍitaḥ śrīmāṁs tat-kaniṣṭha-sahodaraḥ

«Intelligent Śrīvāsa Paṇḍita had previously been Nārada Muni, the best of the sages. Śrīvāsa's younger brother, Śrīmān Rāma Paṇḍita, had previously been Nārada's close friend Parvata Muni.»

## Nārada in the Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā

- Devarṣi Nārada's vīṇā is called **Mahatī** (Sarasvatī's is Kacchapī).
- **Paurṇamāsī** (Yogamāyā), whom Nanda and all of Vraja worship, is Devarṣi Nārada's dear disciple: by her guru's instruction she left her son Sāndīpani, Kṛṣṇa's and Baladeva's teacher, in Avantīpurī and came to Gokula (Bṛhad-bhāga 69–71). Madhumaṅgala and Nāndīmukhī are her grandchildren.
- By Nārada's mercy Kṛṣṇa's messengers Śivadā, Saumya-darśanā, Suprasādā, Sadā-śāntā, Śāntidā and Kāntidā received residence in Vṛndāvana (231–232).

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 90; Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā.

name: Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu
text:
## Who He is

**Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself, Nanda-nandana**, with the mood and complexion of Śrī Rādhā; the *bhakta-rūpa* of the Pañca-tattva, Kṛṣṇa in the form of a devotee.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 10–11

> pañca-tattvātmakaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ bhakta-rūpa-svarūpakam
> bhaktāvatāraṁ bhaktākhyaṁ namāmi bhakta-śaktikam (10)

«I offer my obeisances unto the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa, who is non-different from His features as a devotee, devotional incarnation, devotional manifestation, pure devotee and devotional energy.»

> bhakta-rūpo gauracandro yato 'sau nanda-nandanaḥ
> bhakta-svarūpo nityānando vraje yaḥ śrī-halāyudhaḥ
> bhaktāvatāra ācāryo 'dvaito yaḥ śrī-sadāśivaḥ
> … bhakta-śaktir dvijāgraṇyaḥ śrī-gadādhara-paṇḍitaḥ (11)

Gauracandra is the *bhakta-rūpa* because He is Nanda-nandana; Nityānanda, who is Halāyudha (Balarāma) in Vraja, the *bhakta-svarūpa*; Advaita Ācārya, who is Sadāśiva, the *bhakta-avatāra*; Śrīvāsa and the others the *bhaktas*; Gadādhara Paṇḍita the *bhakta-śakti*.

## Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 58

«The original form of the Supreme Lord is considered not different from His direct expansions: so Lord Caitanya Mahāprabhu, the son of Śrīmatī Śacī-devī, is non-different from Lord Vāsudeva, the first member of the catur-vyūha.»

## Sources

Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 10–11, 58.
replace: Nandgram Dham: Kṛṣṇa Himself, with the mood and complexion of Śrī Rādhā (Caitanya-caritāmṛta Ādi 1.5; Gaura-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā 11).
